proposal.summary: CM550's J1939 receive layer is CM848's. Seven functions are twins: the six input handlers (CM1 / EBC1 / EEC2 / SHUTDN / PTO / CCVS1) match step for step (filter slots, timeout reloads 500 / 50 / 25, data bytes and bit fields, receiver offsets), and the registrar matches except for its capacity (16 entries against CM848's 17). The input registration (it lacks CM848's j1939_input_fault_start_delay = 1000 store) and the tick (only CM848's final count-down loop) are counterparts. The timeout words 0x804234-0x804264 are CM848's j1939_input_signal_timeouts word[25]: the tick walks them and a twin descriptor table at ROM 0x20108 indexes them. The receiver bytes 0x80d70f-0x80d725 are CM848's 23 j1939_received_* bytes at the same e2m 12F7 offsets, all flat bytes. Slot 9 is wet tank pressure in both firmwares' parameter tables, so CM848's 0x40aaba (now accelerator_pedal_position_2) should take the same name.

functions.evidence: FIRST, the one difference: the capacity is 16 here (cmpi.b #16,(0x800b10)) and 17 in CM848 0x538eb0 (cmpwi r7,17). Each is its own table's size (0x800ab0 + 16 x 6 = 0x800b10 and 0x3fd414 + 17 x 6 = 0x3fd47a, the count byte right after the table in both). That is a layout bound, like the different counts and limits of two pairs that already share a name: copyCalibrationFromRomToRam (CM550 0x117ec copies 2401 dwords, CM848 0x4bd00 copies 0x3feed0-0x40a046) and clearWorkingRam (0x2e9ac / 0x538974). If 16 vs 17 counts as a constant, this becomes cm550_registerJ1939ReceiveHandler (a counterpart) and CM848 keeps its name. The steps match: if count == capacity, return 1 (moveq #1 / li r3,1). Otherwise entry = table + count x 6 (d0+d0+d0 then doubled / mulli 6), count + 1, key word to +0 (move.w (8,sp),(a2) / sth r3,0(r6)), handler long to +2 (move.l (10,sp),(2,a2) / stw r4,2(r6)), return 0 (clr.b d0 / li r3,0). CM550's dispatcher 0x212b2 scans the same 6-byte entries up to the count byte (0x21370-0x2137a) and calls +2 with the 18-byte receive record, as CM848's does. RAM dump: count 13, and entries 7-12 are the six input handlers. All 8 call sites push pea handler / move.w #key (clr.w for TSC1). The function transmits nothing, so the old name is wrong. It has no // Function: block in the current .cpp, so this is read from the ROM bytes.

The receive dispatcher 0x212b2 scans count entries for the frame's key and calls the handler. 13 registrations at start-up (13 in the RAM dump). globals.comment: CM848's j1939_input_signal_timeouts (0x3feaa4, word[25]) slot for slot: e2m 12F6 +2n - the MX..TR timers 'TIMER TO TRACK TIME ELAPSED BEFORE <signal> IS RECEIVED AGAIN' (+0 MXMNFMTR manual fan level ... +12 MXWTPRTR wet tank pressure ... +2C MXTESWTR test switch; the parameter ID table tags them EEPROM 0x72a + 2n = 0x803b0a + 0x72a + 2n). The six receive handlers reload slot n when signal n arrives from an accepted source: 500 for slots 0 (CM1) and 10 (SHUTDN), 50 for slots 1-5 (EBC1) and 11-22 (PTO / CCVS1), 25 for slots 6-9 (EEC2); cm550_tickJ1939InputSupervision counts all 25 words down (inclusive bound 0x804264); 0 = the signal timed out. Direct readers: slot 0 cm550_FUN_0002041c (fan request), slot 1 cm550_FUN_00020784 (the remote accelerator - it tests slot 1, the remote accelerator enable switch timer, not slot 8), slot 5 cm550_FUN_00020380 (retarder selection), slot 6 cm550_outputControlState1Handler (idle switch), slot 7 cm550_FUN_00020c98 (pedal position), slot 9 cm550_FUN_00020fac (wet tank pressure); cm550_FUN_00020890 indexes it with j1939_input_signal_descriptor_table's timeout_slot. Slot 23 is 12F6 +2E MXDUMYTR (unused dummy; no writer); slot 24 (0x804264) is a separate record, e2m 11C0 +0 J39PDBLK, reached only through the tick's bound in the dumped ROM - CM848's slot 24 is likewise its history table's length word. Outside the EEPROM mirror 0x803b0a-0x804155, so no _cal. All 0 in the RAM dump (no J1939 input traffic) (PR #53 round 91)
